extracted.intended_audience: State environmental agencies (Maryland), regulated sources (large non-EGUs), EPA reviewers, environmental lawyers, and stakeholders participating in SIP actions
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and requirements used by EPA to evaluate and approve a Maryland State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision reallocating NOx ozone-season emission caps for large non-electric generating units (non-EGUs). Includes statutory/regulatory compliance, monitoring/recordkeeping requirements, incorporation by reference, and procedural/legal limits on the approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory compliance required for SIP approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Clean Air Act, the Administrator is required to approve a SIP submission that complies with the provisions of the Clean Air Act and applicable Federal regulations (42 U.S.C. 7410(k); 40 CFR 52.02(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's role is to approve state choices, provided that they meet the criteria of the Clean Air Act. This action 'merely approves state law as meeting Federal requirements and does not impose additional requirements beyond those imposed by state law.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with NOX SIP Call and 40 CFR 51.121
rubrics_metrics.description: The SIP revision must meet Maryland's NOX SIP Call obligations (including requirements in CAA section 110 and 40 CFR 51.121) for non-EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluated that the June 2024 SIP submittal meets NOX SIP Call obligations by removing an affected source and reallocating its cap; compliance with 40 CFR 51.121 is a basis for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain statewide ozone-season NOX emissions cap
rubrics_metrics.description: The reallocation must not change or alter the specified statewide ozone season NOX emissions cap of 1,013 tons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA found the reallocation 'does not change or alter the specified state-wide ozone season NOX emissions cap of 1,013 tons which is consistent with the portion of the overall Maryland NOX emissions budget under the NOX Budget Trading Program attributable to non-EGUs.' The SIP must preserve the federally-established statewide cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting per 40 CFR part 75 (subpart H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected units are required to perform monitoring under 40 CFR part 75, subpart H in accordance with 40 CFR 51.121(i)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revision 'does not change the 40 CFR part 75 monitoring, recordkeeping and reporting requirements of the original 2018 submission.' SIP approvals must ensure required monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting remain enforceable and consistent with federal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 110(l) non-interference/no-increase requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The SIP revision must not result in increased NOX emissions and therefore must meet section 110(l) of the Clean Air Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA states the June 10, 2024 submittal 'does not result in increased NOX emissions, and therefore has no impact on any requirements related to attainment, reasonable further progress, or any other NAAQS requirements under the CAA. The submittal therefore meets section 110(l) of the CAA.' SIP reviewers should evaluate emissions impacts to ensure non-interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference requirements (1 CFR 51.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: When finalizing regulatory text, EPA must comply with incorporation by reference requirements; here EPA is finalizing the incorporation by reference of Maryland regulation COMAR 26.11.40 in accordance with 1 CFR 51.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA makes incorporated materials generally available through Regulations.gov and at the EPA Region III Office. Materials incorporated by reference become federally enforceable under sections 110 and 113 of the CAA upon approval and incorporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific SIP regulatory text and table identification in 40 CFR 52.1070
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved state regulations and their entries (e.g., COMAR 26.11.40.02 and 26.11.40.03) must be identified and listed in the SIP identification table at §52.1070 (and related 40 CFR citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule revises the table in paragraph (c) of §52.1070 to show state effective dates and EPA approval dates for the specific regulatory provisions being incorporated into the SIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify facility-level NOX ozone-season tonnage caps and new-unit set-aside
rubrics_metrics.description: COMAR 26.11.40 must specify NOX ozone season tonnage caps for affected non-EGU facilities and include a set-aside portion of the statewide cap for new or modified units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule includes a table of NOX season emission caps (e.g., American Sugar Refining C6 = 24 tons; Dominion Energy Cove Point units = 214 tons; NIH unit = 23 tons; New unit set-aside = 752; Total = 1,013). SIP revisions reallocating caps must provide clear, enforceable per-facility caps and set-aside mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing federal trading programs/CSAPR correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: State regulations must reference applicable federal trading programs (e.g., Cross State Air Pollution Rule (CSAPR)) accurately so the state's SIP remains applicable if EPA updates federal rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The June 2024 revision updates cross references to the CSAPR to ensure the state is using a term that will be an applicable reference in the state's SIP if the EPA updates the rule in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic/applicability limits (Indian country exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The SIP approval is not effective on Indian reservation land or other areas where an EPA or Tribe has demonstrated Tribal jurisdiction; SIPs must not be approved to apply in areas where they do not have jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes the SIP 'is not approved to apply on any Indian reservation land or in any other area where the EPA or an Indian Tribe has demonstrated that a Tribe has jurisdiction.' Reviewers should confirm jurisdictional applicability for incorporated provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural/administrative reviews and legal challenge timing
rubrics_metrics.description: SIP approvals are subject to statutory and executive order reviews listed in the preamble (e.g., determinations re: Executive Orders, Paperwork Reduction Act, Regulatory Flexibility Act) and petitions for judicial review must follow section 307(b)(1) of the CAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble lists that the action is not a significant regulatory action under E.O. 12866, does not impose information collection burdens under the PRA, is certified under the RFA, etc. Petitions for judicial review must be filed by the date specified (e.g., Sept 22, 2025 for this action). These are procedural constraints relevant to finalizing and challenging SIP actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA must respond to public comments on NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must respond to comments received on the notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) prior to finalizing the SIP approval; the preamble must address comments and EPA's responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this action EPA notes 'No public comments were received on the NPRM.' When comments are received, EPA's response should be summarized in the preamble explaining how comments were considered in the final decision.
